Finite compact approximation and actual positive licence reserves
2026-10-10. New scoped upper-policy proof/audit; frozen sources unchanged.

0. Conclusion and an explicit correction to the preceding parameter note

The actual adopted upper strategy admits a common finite realization with
positive PREFIX licensing and active-history reserves, and arbitrarily
small density-approximation error. The argument below supplies the missing
quantitative compact-approximation details instead of taking mu>0 as an
unexplained premise. It uses the actual six-branch third envelope, exact
first-exit/subtree identities and the finite, positive-cutoff adopted
modifications. It does not assert a positive minimum on their untrimmed
closed polytopes, or reprove the classical raw Rosser density equalities.

There is one necessary clarification/correction to section4 of
lichtman-common-parameter-selection-20261010.txt. Its equality
  x^(vartheta-2zeta)=T^ell
is an available convenient choice for an already strictly licensed level,
NOT a requirement on every base W-rescue branch. In general the sufficient
condition is
  actual rough support and all relevant squares <= T^ell_aux
       = x^(vartheta-2zeta),
  ell_actual+endpoint inflation <= ell_aux.                 (C0)
The auxiliary exponent ell_aux may be slightly ABOVE the actual frozen
density cap. The W construction below requires this freedom near its gate.
It is the original source's intermediate factorization parameter, not an
increase of the raw tree cap. All density sums, histories, coefficients
rho and saved integrals continue to use the SAME actual cap lambda.

The greedy support proof is monotone in this upper bound: a full-square
inequality at T^lambda is also true at the larger T^ell_aux, and the
whole-slot assignment uses only those inequalities and its licensed
capacities. Its three monomial bounds concern the auxiliary D, which is
chosen with strict surplus below the branch endpoint. Therefore (C0)
preserves the existing signed coefficient and does not replace it with a
different density weight. No old file is edited by this clarification.

1. Exact base functions and a uniform approximation bound

Use distinct notation throughout:
  rho=19/96, mu0=25/128, Lambda=153/256, Theta=299/500,
  A(s)=(1+s)/2, D(s)=57/64-3s/2, v(s)=min(A(s),D(s)),
  W(z)=Lambda-3z/8.
On 0<=z<=y<=x<=mu0 the true gated envelope equals
  L3=max(v(x),v(x+y),v(x+z),v(y+z),v(x+y+z),W(z)).           (C1)
At x>mu0 the current base uses v(x), not this full formula.
This is the ordered-envelope identity, not permission to remove arbitrary
selected gates. I recheck the two ingredients used in finite approximation.

For a nonleading pair, put (s,r)=(x+z,y) or(y+z,x). If v(s)>=v(x), then
  v(s)-(s+2r)>=gamma,       gamma=3/256.                    (C2)
For s<=mu0 this is 1/2-s/2-2r>=1/2-5mu0/2. For s>=mu0,
v(s)>=A(x) implies s<=(25/32-x)/3, so the difference is at least
23/96-7x/6>=3/256. A pair below v(x) cannot affect the maximum.
The two W inner minima reduce to W(z) and W(y), since
(66-34u)/107-W(u)=525/27392+49u/856>0 and
1-2y>=39/64>Lambda. Their common gate is A(x). Hence their contribution
TO THE MAXIMUM is max(A(x),W(z)); one does not claim an ungated W action
at every point. These computations prove the actual gated interpretation
of (C1), including its ties.

Let B be any closed ordered coarse triple box of coordinate width<=chi,
contained in x<=mu0. Every branch in (C1) is9/2-Lipschitz in the sup
norm; the pair-gate differences are7-Lipschitz. Use the original Gamma_B
rule: maxima of the indicated branch infima, max(A,W) for a W rescue,
and include a nonleading pair only when its whole-box gate gap>=e.
Choose e<gamma/100 and chi<min(e/10,gamma/28).

If a pair realizes the maximum at a point of B, (C2) shows that its
gate gap everywhere on B is at least gamma-7chi>=3gamma/4>e.
It is therefore included. All other maximizing branches are included
unconditionally. Each included continuous branch is bounded by L3.
Taking its infimum loses at most(9/2)chi. Consequently, UNIFORMLY on B,
  0<=L3(t)-Gamma_B<=(9/2)chi.                              (C3)
This holds even on a branch tie. It is not merely an almost-everywhere
convergence argument, and it needs no positive lower cutoff on z.

The extended construction retains first labels with upper endpoint
<=rho-4e and uses the full Gamma_B rule only on boxes wholly below
x=mu0-4e. Otherwise it uses inf_B v(x). On the transition portion below
mu0 we have x>=mu0-4e-chi and
  0<=L3-v(x)<=Lambda-A(x)<=2e+chi/2.
Above mu0 the fallback is exactly v(x). Since every branch is<=Lambda
and Theta-Lambda=11/32000>0, the extended cap is simply
  lambda_B=Gamma_B-2e < nu=Theta-2e.                       (C4)
The minimum in the original formula is redundant here. Combining (C3)
and the transition estimate gives a safe global bound
  0<=L_endpoint-lambda_B<=4e+6chi                          (C5)
on every retained ordered triple. Its first cube has positive margin:
below mu0, v(x)-3x>=gamma; near rho the cutoff gives
v(x)-3x>=18e, so lambda_B-3x>=16e-O(chi)>15e.

2. Producing a real licence reserve, including the W gate

Freeze e,chi and the finite Gamma_B list before the rough cutoff. The
actual cap is always lambda_B. For factorization choose an auxiliary
level on the SAME coarse box, then retain it on its fine refinements.
Only fixed rational choices and finitely many branch labels are needed.

For a maximizing ordinary v branch, the selected endpoint is at least
Gamma_B. Choose ell_aux=lambda_B+e/4. Leading-product and singleton
complement squares are supplied by the actual full support/first cube;
nonleading pairs that can be needed have the stronger(C2) whole-box
reserve, not merely the inclusion threshold e. For e,chi as above these
gates are below ell_aux. The tent licence retains more than e surplus
after taking vartheta=q ell_aux+2zeta with zeta and|q-1| sufficiently
small compared with e. If a nonleading pair is everywhere dominated by
A(x), choose the baseline label instead; it is not needed as a licence.

For a maximizing rescue entry F=max(A(x),W_i), inf_B F=Gamma_B, use this
explicit whole-box dichotomy (A oscillates by at most chi/2):

  (i) inf_B A >= lambda_B+e/2.
      Set ell_aux=lambda_B+e/4 and use the singleton-largest licence.
      At q=1,2zeta<e/20 leaves at least e/5 below A throughout B.

  (ii) inf_B A < lambda_B+e/2.
      Then sup_B A < lambda_B+11e/20, since chi<e/10.
      As max(A,W_i)>=Gamma_B=lambda_B+2e at every point, W_i>=Gamma_B
      everywhere. Set ell_aux=lambda_B+e. It exceeds the W gate by
      at least9e/20 and lies e below W_i. The other initial-prime
      square has the independent reserve
      1-Lambda-2mu0=3/256. The other third-slot inner branch has the
      positive margin525/8704+49t3/272 at W(t3). Thus small zeta,
      coordinate perturbations and fine endpoint inflation preserve
      all the repaired W initialization and continuation inequalities.

This is why requiring every W gate to lie below the ACTUAL lambda_B
would be too strong. Case(ii) may have A>lambda_B. Enlarging only the
analytic support envelope as in(C0) solves this without modifying lambda_B.
It also explains why the exact equality convention in the previous common
